newsitem.title: USA: U.S West Coast Lt. crudes fall, heavies still weak.
newsitem.headline: U.S West Coast Lt. crudes fall, heavies still weak.

text.p: U.S. West Coast light crude prices fell with lower heating oil futures Tuesday, while heavy California grades remained weaker in an oversupplied market, traders said.
The region's traders said heavy crude barrels moved east over the crowded All-American pipeline, or were offered to makers of heavy fuel oil.
"Whatever's moving is moving at a loss," a trader said, citing an unconfirmed deal Friday at $1.00 under postings.
Earlier last week heavies sold at 25 to 50 cents under postings.
The region's excess oil was meant to run at Tosco's Avon, Calif., refinery until a fire late last month cut intake.

Confirmed prices for San Joaquin Valley heavies ranged $17 to 17.25 a barrel on Tuesday. So far, traders saw no major price shifts on lighter Valley grades, which are bought to pump heavies through pipelines.
Meanwhile, traders shrugged off a weekend explosion at Paramount's Los Angeles refinery, noting the plant -- at a 46,000 bpd capacity -- was too small to impact crude supplies.
The Alaskan crude market remained quiet, while traders at BP -- the grade's dominant seller --attended a company meeting.
Outright ANS prices fell 30 cents to $22.35/22.55 a barrel, weighed by a heating oil market which dropped on expected supply builds.
